strings.cfg:biomes/caves/desc: The legacy of the Empire of Blood and Beast — rotting forest depths, underground menageries and ritual pits. The realm set out to make the perfect soldier by mixing the blood of men, beasts and magical creatures. First came mighty warriors, then packs, then a hunger that cannot be stopped. The underground laboratories became the lairs of cursed beastmen and mutated creatures.
strings.cfg:biomes/crypt/desc: The legacy of the Empire of the Dead Crown — catacombs, necropolises and imperial tombs. That realm feared oblivion above all else: its rulers poured their wealth into necromancy, into preserving bodies and raising immortal legions, so their dynasties might rule forever. Its mages learned to bring the dead back, but not to bring back the soul — whole cities became necropolises, and the eternal army became will-less undead.
strings.cfg:biomes/dungeon/desc: The legacy of the Empire of the Aetheric Archives — underground reactors, crystal towers, libraries of spells and machines that hold the aether in place. The realm staked everything on pure magical science, certain that magic could be measured, divided and stored as fuel. But magic proved to be a living force: the archives began to think for themselves, the machines slipped the leash, and the spells came into a will of their own.
strings.cfg:biomes/dungeon/tagline: "Man became surplus to his own creation."
strings.cfg:biomes/labyrinth/desc: The legacy of the Empire of the Rift — demons, cultists, warped architecture and portals to the lower planes. That realm went further than any other: its rulers tore rifts open, struck bargains with demons and called up things from beyond the edge of reality as weapons against the other realms. But the demons did not come to serve — they came to collect. The deepest levels already belong, in part, to another dimension.
strings.cfg:biomes/labyrinth/tagline: "You cannot be the master of an element — you are only its instrument."

strings.cfg:run-modifiers/greedy-vault/desc: Gold from the run is increased by 25%.
strings.cfg:run-modifiers/relic-greed/desc: +15% drop bias for the whole run.
strings.cfg:run-modifiers/relic-vitality/desc: The player gains +10% maximum health for the whole run.
strings.cfg:seals/cursed-descent/desc: More magic and rare monsters — and rarer finds.
strings.cfg:seals/enduring/desc: Monsters are tougher, but grant more experience.
strings.cfg:seals/furious/desc: Monster blows hurt more, but loot rarity is higher.
strings.cfg:seals/lair/desc: One room of the floor becomes a lair: its whole pack is rare monsters, and the finds are richer.
strings.cfg:seals/onslaught/desc: Monsters strike more often — and drop more items.
strings.cfg:seals/pursuit/desc: Monsters are faster — and carry more gold.
strings.cfg:seals/swarming/desc: Packs are larger, and the slain drop more items.
strings.cfg:seals/warden/desc: A champion joins the floor's pack: a unique at "mini" rank with a level bonus; it grants more experience too.
strings.cfg:skill-insert-types/ailment/descripti: What it leaves behind on a hit: burning, chill, bleeding, poison.
strings.cfg:skill-insert-types/area/description: Who gets caught: arc, range, radius, projectile spread, pierce, a series of blows.
strings.cfg:skill-insert-types/companion/descrip: A second effect on use: a wave, a chain, an extra blow.
strings.cfg:skill-insert-types/control/descripti: What it does to the target besides damage: knockback, stun, knockdown.
strings.cfg:skill-insert-types/damage/descriptio: How hard it hits and with what: multiplier, an element folded into the base damage, conversion.
strings.cfg:skill-insert-types/hunt/description: A bonus under a condition: against undead, against burning targets, at low health. These inserts will appear once target conditions reach the hit path.
strings.cfg:skill-insert-types/sigil/description: An effect on YOURSELF when used: a shield, haste, recovery.
strings.cfg:skill-insert-types/tempo/description: More often, cheaper, faster — always at the cost of something else.
strings.cfg:skill-inserts/ins-arc-burst/descript: On use, it shocks everyone standing right beside you.
strings.cfg:skill-inserts/ins-blood-rhythm/descr: The more bleeding enemies around you, the faster your blows: +8% speed for each, up to five.
strings.cfg:skill-inserts/ins-cold-wave/descript: On use, a wave of cold spreads out and binds everyone nearby.
strings.cfg:skill-inserts/ins-flame-edge/descrip: A third of the skill's damage is added as fire, on top of its usual make-up.
strings.cfg:skill-inserts/ins-flurry/description: Two blows instead of one, each at half strength.
strings.cfg:skill-inserts/ins-frost-edge/descrip: A third of the skill's damage is added as cold, on top of its usual make-up.
strings.cfg:skill-inserts/ins-heavy-blow/descrip: Damage ×1.4, but the skill costs noticeably more and comes off cooldown slower.
strings.cfg:skill-inserts/ins-hoarfrost/descript: A third of hits bind the target with cold — it moves slower.
strings.cfg:skill-inserts/ins-kindling/descripti: A third of hits set the target alight.
strings.cfg:skill-inserts/ins-piercing/descripti: The projectile passes through the target and flies on.
strings.cfg:skill-inserts/ins-quickening/descrip: The cooldown is nearly a third shorter — at the cost of damage.
strings.cfg:skill-inserts/ins-serrated/descripti: A third of hits leave a bleed.
strings.cfg:skill-inserts/ins-sweep/description: A sizeable chance to knock the target off its feet.
strings.cfg:skill-inserts/ins-swiftness/descript: On use, hastens you for a few seconds — no more than once every 10.5 s (sigil cooldown).
strings.cfg:skill-inserts/ins-thrift/description: The skill costs noticeably less — at the cost of damage.
strings.cfg:skill-inserts/ins-ward/description: On use, covers you in armour for a few seconds — no more than once every 14 s (sigil cooldown).
strings.cfg:skill-inserts/ins-wide-arc/descripti: The arc is wider and reaches further, but every blow is weaker.

strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-balestrino/lore: The balestrino — a tiny all-steel Italian crossbow of the 16th–18th c.: the spanning screw is hidden in the hollow grip, and the whole crossbow fitted within one's clothes.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-barrel/caption: cosmetic for now: does not affect the projectile
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-barrel/lore: The slurbow — a crossbow with a "barrel" over the groove: it appears in English inventories from the early 16th c.; an early surviving example, kept in Madrid, is dated 1549.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-cheek/caption: cosmetic for now: does not affect the projectile
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-cheek/lore: Halbe Rüstung ("half harness") — the standard German hunting crossbow of c. 1540–1750: a shortened stock with a cheek butt, a schneller lock, spanned by cranequin.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-chu-repeater/capt: cosmetic for now: does not affect the projectile
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-chu-repeater/lore: A double-shot crossbow from the Chu tomb Qinjiazui M47 (4th c. BC): 20 bolts, two per shot, 20–25 m — more likely a nobleman's piece for self-defence or fowling.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-cranequin/caption: cosmetic for now: does not affect the projectile
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-cranequin/lore: A short stock, widened at the lock, with a cross-pin for the cranequin's loop, c. 1460–1480 (Payne-Gallwey 1903); the oldest dated crossbow of this kind belonged to Ulrich V of Württemberg, 1460.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-ganze/caption: cosmetic for now: does not affect the projectile
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-ganze/lore: Ganze Rüstung ("full harness") — the largest German hand crossbow of the 16th–17th c.; sources disagree whether it was used for hunting or only shot at contests.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-gastraphetes/capt: cosmetic for now: does not affect the projectile
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-gastraphetes/lore: The gastraphetes — a Greek "belly bow", known by 399 BC at the latest: the archer leaned his belly into a concave rest and drove the slider back along a ratchet.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-kugel/caption: cosmetic for now: does not affect the projectile
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-kugel/lore: The kugelschnepper — a German ball-shooting crossbow of the first half of the 17th c.: a straight iron column with a fitted butt and a spanning lever right on the stock.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-lady-stonebow/cap: cosmetic for now: does not affect the projectile
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-lady-stonebow/lor: Per Payne-Gallwey, the lightest "ladies'" stonebows of the 16th c. were held and aimed with one hand, though the string was spanned with two.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-narrow/caption: cosmetic for now: does not affect the projectile
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-narrow/lore: "One-foot" (arbalista ad unum pedem) — in Payne-Gallwey's reading, a narrow stirrup for a single foot; that reading was later revised (G. Wilson, 2007).
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-pistol/caption: cosmetic for now: does not affect the projectile
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-pistol/lore: The pistol crossbow for indoor shooting of the early 19th c. copies the pistol of its day; Breiding counts such crossbows direct descendants of the balestrino.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-rampart/caption: cosmetic for now: does not affect the projectile
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-rampart/lore: The rampart crossbow (Wallarmbrust) of the 15th c. weighed 8–9 kg, so it was shot from a parapet or a tripod; per Payne-Gallwey, only a very strong man could shoot it from the shoulder.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-schnepper/caption: cosmetic for now: does not affect the projectile
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-schnepper/lore: The schnepper — a light Saxon hunting and target crossbow of the 17th–18th c.: a musket butt, a catch instead of a nut, spanned with a detachable push lever.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-shenbi/caption: cosmetic for now: does not affect the projectile
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-shenbi/lore: "Divine Arm" (神臂弓) — a heavy Song crossbow presented to the court in 1068–1077: a stock of mountain mulberry, an iron stirrup; per Shen Kuo, it struck at three hundred paces.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-spanish/caption: cosmetic for now: does not affect the projectile
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-spanish/lore: The Spanish ballesta: per Espinar (1644), the perfect crossbow is one whose stock runs straight "from the head to the end of the grip"; deer were hunted with it until about 1635.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-stonebow/caption: cosmetic for now: does not affect the projectile
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-stonebow/lore: An Italian stonebow of the 16th c. (arbalète à jalet): the fore of the stock bends down, so that a pebble or ball from the double string's pouch flies clear over it.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-target/caption: cosmetic for now: does not affect the projectile
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-target/lore: A guild target crossbow of Belgium and the Netherlands, 17th–19th c.: a heavy stock with a projection beneath for the left hand — a grip per Payne-Gallwey, a rest per museum descriptions.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-vgrip/caption: cosmetic for now: does not affect the projectile
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-vgrip/lore: The army nu of the Qin and Han: a straight stock with no butt, a bronze trigger with a "wangshan" sight, held by a vertical grip under the lock.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-waist/caption: cosmetic for now: does not affect the projectile
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-waist/lore: The Ming "腰開弩" ("spanned by the waist") per the "Wubei Zhi" (1621): a short stock for an enormous prod, spanned seated, with the feet and a belt hook; its dimensions are known only as recalculated by a secondary source.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-wide/caption: cosmetic for now: does not affect the projectile
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-wide/lore: "Two-foot" (ad duos pedes) — per Payne-Gallwey, a wide stirrup for both feet, for the stiff prods of the 13th–14th c.; that reading was later revised (G. Wilson, 2007).
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-windlass/caption: cosmetic for now: does not affect the projectile
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-windlass/lore: Windlass crossbow à moulinet, 15th c.: a long stock with no butt, the windlass box fitted over its tail; per Payne-Gallwey, spanning took ≈12 s.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-zhuge/caption: cosmetic for now: does not affect the projectile
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/cb-st-zhuge/lore: The Zhuge nu — a repeating crossbow of the Ming and Qing; the "Tiangong Kaiwu" (1637) calls it a household guard against thieves, not a weapon of war.

strings.cfg:weapon-parts/st-crook/lore: "A crooked staff without knots" — Livy I.18.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/st-fork/caption: most frequent discharges in the pool
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/st-orb/lore: Ferula — a staff topped with an orb (Catholic Encyclopedia 1908).
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/st-serpents/lore: In Rus from the mid-17th c., under Nikon.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/st-skull/caption: most frequent discharges in the pool
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/st-tau/lore: A tau crook; emblem of the Antonines.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-a-falchion/caption: heavier in the hand: bigger hits
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-a-falchion/lore: A single-edged blade widening towards the end: its weight goes where it meets the target.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-a-sabre/caption: fastest in the pool: more ailments and procs
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-a-sabre/lore: A slightly curved single-edged blade: it cuts with a draw, not a blow.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-a-x/lore: Type X: broad, fullered along its whole length, the point rounded. A blade of the Early Age: for cutting, not thrusting.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-a-xi/caption: lighter in the hand: faster pace, smaller hits
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-a-xi/lore: Type XI: a long, narrow blade with a narrow fuller — light in the hand, quick to recover.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-a-xii/lore: Type XII: the blade tapers evenly, fullered for two-thirds of its length. The measure all others are reckoned from.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-a-xiii/caption: heavier in the hand: bigger hits
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-a-xiii/lore: Type XIII: a broad blade, parallel edges, a rounded point. A sword for a hand used to the shield.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-a-xix/caption: fastest in the pool: more ailments and procs
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-a-xix/lore: Type XIX: a narrow blade of hexagonal section, with a short ricasso for the finger.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-a-xv/caption: fastest in the pool: more ailments and procs
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-a-xv/lore: Type XV: diamond section, tapering straight to the point. Forged against armour, not against leather.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-a-xvi/caption: lighter in the hand: faster pace, smaller hits
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-a-xvi/lore: Type XVI: the upper half fullered, the lower half drawn to a diamond. Half the blade cuts, half thrusts.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-a-xviii/caption: heavier in the hand: bigger hits
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-a-xviii/lore: Type XVIII: diamond section, broad at the base. Tapered to slip into the joints of armour.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-g-xiia/lore: Type XIIa: a lengthened XII for a hand and a half.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-g-xiiia/lore: Type XIIIa: a broad blade with parallel edges on a long grip.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-g-xva/caption: fastest in the pool: more ailments and procs
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-g-xva/lore: Type XVa: a narrow thrusting blade, drawn to a diamond from base to point.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-g-xvii/caption: lighter in the hand: faster pace, smaller hits
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-g-xvii/lore: Type XVII: hexagonal section with no fuller — the blade is stiff along its whole length.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-g-xx/caption: heavier in the hand: bigger hits
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-g-xx/lore: Type XX: a broad blade with two or three fullers — the weight taken off in strips.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-gd-claymore/lore: The quillons slope towards the blade and end in quatrefoils: they catch an enemy's edge and keep it from the hand.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-gd-curved/lore: The ends curve towards the blade: an enemy's edge slides off rather than biting into the guard.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-gd-figured/lore: Flared, ornate ends: the work of a master who had time to spare.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-gd-long/lore: A long, straight crossguard — the yardstick for all the rest; the whole Classical Age rests on it.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-gd-nagel/lore: The nagel — a side spike — guards the fingers where the crossguard is short.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-gd-rings/lore: Side rings and parrying hooks — a hilt of the Empire.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-gd-shield/lore: A guard plate before the grip: an archaic ward for the hand, simple and sound.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-gd-short/lore: A short, straight crossguard of the Early Age: it covers the fingers and keeps clear of the shield.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-gr-cramped/caption: close in, but with the widest sweep
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-gr-hand-half/caption: a little farther, a little narrower
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-gr2-short/caption: close in, but with the widest sweep
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-h-narrow/caption: fastest in the pool: more ailments and procs
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-h-narrow/lore: A long, narrow blade with a long ricasso for a second grip: a two-hander that thrusts.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-h-straight/lore: The straight blade of a two-hander with no ricasso: nothing superfluous, everything in the length.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-h-wavy/caption: lighter in the hand: faster pace, smaller hits
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-h-wavy/lore: Wavy edges: such a blade comes only from a master's hand, and only from good steel.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-h-wide/lore: An unsharpened base for the second hand: the blade can be gripped short and worked like a polearm.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-pm-ball/lore: A ball pommel of the Archaic Age: cast in one piece, with nothing to break.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-pm-brazil/lore: A nut-shaped pommel: the Early Age passed, but this shape held on longest of all.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-pm-disc/caption: steadier under blows — higher Block, fewer ailments
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-pm-disc/lore: A disc pommel: the most common in the Classical Age and the cheapest to repair.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-pm-faceted/lore: A faceted pommel of the Empire: its corners grip the wielder's hand and tear another's.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-pm-fishtail/lore: A "fishtail" pommel of the Empire: forked and spread across the palm.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-pm-lobed/lore: A three- or five-lobed pommel of the Early Age: cast, and divided into lobes.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-pm-pear/lore: A pear-shaped pommel of the Empire: its weight sinks down the tang.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-pm-spiked/caption: its damage type's ailment more often — lower Block
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-pm-spiked/lore: A spike instead of a counterweight: no such pommels were forged anywhere — this one was devised here.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-pm-triangular/lore: A triangular pommel of the Early Age — a simple wedge casting on the tang.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-pm-wheel/lore: A disc with bevelled edges: the same as a disc, but a gram lighter and a day's work dearer.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-r-backed/caption: lighter in the hand: faster pace, smaller hits
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-r-backed/lore: A straight, thick back and a single edge. Half knife, half sword — and cheaper than either.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-r-blunt/caption: heavier in the hand: bigger hits
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-r-blunt/lore: Parallel edges, the end cut off blunt: this blade needs no point — it cuts.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-r-cast/caption: heavier in the hand: bigger hits
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-r-cast/lore: Cast in one piece with the hilt. It breaks along the casting, but any smith can make one.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-r-falling/lore: The blade leans forward and grows heavy towards the end: it falls into the target by itself — just hold on.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-r-fulham/caption: lighter in the hand: faster pace, smaller hits
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-r-fulham/lore: The edges run straight, the point cut to a triangle. Simpler to forge than the rest — and chosen for it.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-r-hisp/lore: The longest of the archaic blades, with a waist midway along it: the hand feels where it wants to cut.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-r-leaf/caption: heavier in the hand: bigger hits
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-r-leaf/lore: The blade swells to the middle and narrows to the point — its weight goes where it meets the target.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-r-mainz/caption: heavier in the hand: bigger hits
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-r-mainz/lore: A broad blade and a long point, the edges converging gently. A blade for the line, where men thrust more often than they cut.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-r-needle/caption: fastest in the pool: more ailments and procs
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-r-needle/lore: A long, narrow blade with almost no cutting edge: it pierces clean through and bends on bone.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-r-pompeii/caption: fastest in the pool: more ailments and procs
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-r-pompeii/lore: Parallel edges and a short point. The cheapest of the archaic blades: they were forged by the cartload.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-r-sickle/lore: Sharpened on the outer curve. There is nothing to thrust with: it hooks behind the shield and pulls.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-r-stub/caption: lighter in the hand: faster pace, smaller hits
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-r-stub/lore: The shortest blade still called a sword. Worn at the belt by those who fought on horseback.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-r-tongue/caption: lighter in the hand: faster pace, smaller hits
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-r-tongue/lore: The edges run straight and close sharply into a tongue at the very tip: it cuts with the blade and thrusts with the point.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-r-watered/lore: The blade is twisted from rods and etched: the pattern shows in the light and survives sharpening.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-s-xiiib/lore: Type XIIIb: the edges almost parallel — the shortened measure of a cutting blade.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-s-xiv/caption: fastest in the pool: more ailments and procs
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-s-xiv/lore: Type XIV: broad at the base, tapering sharply to the point. It cuts and thrusts alike, and either is foul for whoever it strikes.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/sw-s-xxii/lore: Type XXII: a broad blade with two short fullers at the base. Heavy in the hand, and the more fearsome for it.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/wd-fang/caption: finer focus: more frequent, smaller discharges
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/wd-fang/lore: Egyptian apotropaic "wands" of the Middle Kingdom — a ward, not a venom.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/wd-fork/caption: most frequent discharges in the pool
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/wd-fork/lore: A forked hazel rod — the "Verge foudroyante" of the Grand Grimoire.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/wd-hand/lore: The "hand of justice" of the French kings.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/wd-orb/lore: An orb: a sign of power.
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/wd-prism/caption: finer focus: more frequent, smaller discharges
strings.cfg:weapon-parts/wd-prism/lore: A wand with a prism — Éliphas Lévi, 19th c.

strings.cfg:weapon-types/axe/names/ax-vi/subtitl: two pairs of lugs, plain poll

strings.cfg:weapon-types/bow/names/bw-composite/: horn, sinew and wood; stiff siyah tips

strings.cfg:weapon-types/crossbow/names/cb-chu-r: Qinjiazui M47, 4th c. BC: 20 bolts, two per shot
strings.cfg:weapon-types/crossbow/names/cb-crane: rack spanning; slower than a windlass — 35 s against 12
strings.cfg:weapon-types/crossbow/names/cb-ganze: Ganze Rüstung ("full harness"): Rechenberg, 1663 — 83 cm, 11.7 kg
strings.cfg:weapon-types/crossbow/names/cb-gastr: "belly bow": ratcheted slider, belly rest; no later than 399 BC
strings.cfg:weapon-types/crossbow/names/cb-germa: Halbe Rüstung, c. 1540–1750: cheek butt, schneller trigger, cranequin
strings.cfg:weapon-types/crossbow/names/cb-goats: a "goat's foot" lever, from the mid-14th c.
strings.cfg:weapon-types/crossbow/names/cb-han-n: army nu of the Qin–Han: bronze lock with a "wangshan" sight, vertical grip
strings.cfg:weapon-types/crossbow/names/cb-kugel: ball-shooting: iron column, fitted butt, lever on the stock; Germany, 1600–1650
strings.cfg:weapon-types/crossbow/names/cb-lady-: so light it was aimed with one hand; 16th c.
strings.cfg:weapon-types/crossbow/names/cb-one-f: arbalista ad unum pedem — as read by Payne-Gallwey; in Old Rus, the "stirrup crossbow"
strings.cfg:weapon-types/crossbow/names/cb-pisto: indoor shooting, 19th c.; per Breiding, a descendant of the balestrino
strings.cfg:weapon-types/crossbow/names/cb-rampa: Wallarmbrust, 15th c.: 125 cm, 8.6 kg; shot from a parapet or a tripod
strings.cfg:weapon-types/crossbow/names/cb-samos: Old Rus: a stirrup at the fore of the stock, a loose nut; in the chronicles from 1159
strings.cfg:weapon-types/crossbow/names/cb-schne: light Saxon, 17th–18th c.: musket butt, a catch instead of a nut, push lever
strings.cfg:weapon-types/crossbow/names/cb-shenb: 神臂弓, "Divine Arm": iron stirrup, stock ≈1 m; Song, 1068–1077
strings.cfg:weapon-types/crossbow/names/cb-slurb: barrelled crossbow: an unfletched bolt in a slotted barrel; Madrid, 1549
strings.cfg:weapon-types/crossbow/names/cb-spani: Spanish: straight stock, iron cheeks by the nut, gafa lever; Espinar, 1644
with a western ("Spanish") cranequin: rack teeth up; 15th–17th c.
strings.cfg:weapon-types/crossbow/names/cb-stone: stonebow, arbalète à jalet: stock bent downwards, a ball shot from the pouch of a double string; 16th–17th c.
strings.cfg:weapon-types/crossbow/names/cb-targe: guild shooting at targets and the "popinjay", 17th–19th c.; a rest under the stock for the left hand
strings.cfg:weapon-types/crossbow/names/cb-waist: 腰開弩, Ming: ≈52 cm stock for a ≈195 cm prod, spanned seated with a belt hook
strings.cfg:weapon-types/crossbow/names/cb-windl: spanned à moulinet / à tour, 15th c.; ≈12 s per spanning
strings.cfg:weapon-types/crossbow/names/cb-zhuge: 諸葛弩: magazine of 10–12 bolts; the lever both spans and looses; Ming–Qing

strings.cfg:weapon-types/dagger/names/dg-baselar: H-shaped hilt; probably named after Basel
strings.cfg:weapon-types/dagger/names/dg-quillon: quillon dagger: quillons and a sword-style pommel — the hilt copies a sword's
strings.cfg:weapon-types/dagger/names/dg-rondel/: dagger with discs at both ends of the grip, 15th c.
strings.cfg:weapon-types/dagger/names/dg-scramas: guardless fighting knife, up to 50 cm
strings.cfg:weapon-types/dagger/names/dg-stilett: faceted blade on a rondel hilt
strings.cfg:weapon-types/halberd/names/hb-early-: Sichelbarte: blade mounted on two rings
strings.cfg:weapon-types/halberd/names/hb-glaive: a knife blade on a shaft
strings.cfg:weapon-types/halberd/names/hb-partis: broad thrusting head of the spear family
strings.cfg:weapon-types/halberd/names/hb-poleax: axe and beak on a shaft
axe and hammer on a shaft, against 15th-c. plate
strings.cfg:weapon-types/halberd/names/hb-spetum: narrow spike and two side prongs
strings.cfg:weapon-types/halberd/names/hb-vouge-: narrow single-edged blade on a socket, langets and rondel, France, 15th c.
strings.cfg:weapon-types/halberd/names/hb-vouge/: narrow single-edged blade on a socket
strings.cfg:weapon-types/spear/names/sp-halfpike: a pike held at the middle
strings.cfg:weapon-types/spear/names/sp-long/sub: broad head on a long shaft
strings.cfg:weapon-types/spear/names/sp-rogatina: heavy head and a crossbar to stop a beast
strings.cfg:weapon-types/spear/names/sp-trident/: Europe knew no one-handed war trident
strings.cfg:weapon-types/spear/names/sp-twospike: two-pronged head on a long shaft
strings.cfg:weapon-types/staff/names/st-archbish: an orb on a knop, knops along the shaft
strings.cfg:weapon-types/staff/names/st-serpents: the bronze serpent of Moses; in Rus from the mid-17th c.
strings.cfg:weapon-types/staff/names/st-tau/subt: emblem of the Antonines; "St Anthony's fire" is ergot poisoning
strings.cfg:weapon-types/sword/fallback/subtitle: irregular pattern: the Codex lists no such combination
strings.cfg:weapon-types/sword/names/sw-bastard/: a grip for a second hand: a one-handed blade taken in both
strings.cfg:weapon-types/sword/names/sw-caroling: broad blade, short crossguard, lobed pommel
strings.cfg:weapon-types/sword/names/sw-claymore: sloping quillons ending in quatrefoils, and a wheel pommel
strings.cfg:weapon-types/sword/names/sw-falchion: single-edged blade, widening towards the end
strings.cfg:weapon-types/sword/names/sw-flammens: waves along both edges: it tears rather than cuts
strings.cfg:weapon-types/sword/names/sw-gladius/: infantry blade of the Archaic Age: guard plate and ball pommel
strings.cfg:weapon-types/sword/names/sw-great/su: long crossguard and heavy pommel: the measure all others follow
strings.cfg:weapon-types/sword/names/sw-khopesh/: a sickle edged on the outer curve: it hooks behind the shield and pulls
strings.cfg:weapon-types/sword/names/sw-kopis/su: the blade leans forward: it cuts with its weight, not the wrist
strings.cfg:weapon-types/sword/names/sw-messer/s: single-edged blade with grip scales and a side spike by the hand
strings.cfg:weapon-types/sword/names/sw-romanesq: long crossguard and heavy pommel of the Classical Age
strings.cfg:weapon-types/sword/names/sw-sabre/su: slightly curved: it cuts with a draw, not a blow
strings.cfg:weapon-types/sword/names/sw-seax/sub: single-edged, with a straight thick back
strings.cfg:weapon-types/sword/names/sw-short-kn: short blade, curved crossguard, wheel pommel
strings.cfg:weapon-types/sword/names/sw-spatha/s: long straight cavalry blade: it cuts from the saddle
strings.cfg:weapon-types/sword/names/sw-xiphos/s: cast leaf blade with a high midrib on a short crossguard
strings.cfg:weapon-types/sword/names/sw-zweihand: two-hander of the Empire: ricasso for a second grip, rings and hooks
strings.cfg:weapon-types/wand/names/wd-fang/subt: apotropaic "wand" of the Middle Kingdom — a ward, not a venom
strings.cfg:weapon-types/wand/names/wd-prism/sub: a magus's wand after Éliphas Lévi
strings.cfg:weapon-types/wand/names/wd-thunder/s: Verge foudroyante: a fork of wild hazel
